newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch discover outbreak of swine fever.
newsitem.headline: Dutch discover outbreak of swine fever.

text.p: Dutch government said on Tuesday it had discovered an outbreak of swine fever in the south of the country and as a precaution had closed off the one farm involved and two nearby slaughterhouses.
A spokewoman told Reuters all the pigs at the farm and carcasses still held at the slaughterhouses were being destroyed pending an investigation by Dutch agriculture authorities.
It was too early to say if there would be any ban on pig exports, she added.

On Monday, Germany decided to ban the export of pigs for slaughter from four regional states affected by the disease. Authorities there have already ordered the slaughter of 14,000 pigs to try and contain the outbreak and Belgium has banned all German pig imports.
The Netherlands suffered its last outbreak of swine fever, which is not harmful to humans, in 1992.
